body.statement: For every \((\theta,M,P_{\mathrm{obs}},W,\mathcal G(W,\ell))\in\mathfrak M_{p,q,\ell}^{\mathrm{Yang}}(\mathbb R)\), the label-restricted recovered candidate sets are pairwise disjoint and \(V=(\bigsqcup_{g=1}^{k}R_g)\sqcup V_{\mathrm{fix}}(\mathcal G,\ell)\). Hence \(g_{\mathcal G,\ell}(u)\) is defined uniquely for every \(u\in V\). If \(g_{\mathcal G,\ell}(u)=g\in[k]\), then \(u\) is the cogent center in a legal completion exactly when \(r_g=u\), and otherwise it is an mleaf in that group. If \(g_{\mathcal G,\ell}(u)=\bot\), then \(u\) is a fixed singleton mleaf in every legal completion.
body.justification: A total label-to-group map is necessary to bind the group index in every intervention-specific image and to separate switchable group members from fixed singleton mleafs.
body.gap: Yang et al. recover label-restricted AOG groups, but the effect layer requires the induced per-label partition and fixed-mleaf branch to be stated explicitly.
body.consumer: The partition makes every subsequent intervention-specific effect set a well-defined function of its displayed arguments.
